doc.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Playing with his brother Sam
summary: Abe and Sam play together in his big band; they were distant for years but became buddies in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Absolutely. Now you get to play with Sam on occasion.

As a matter of fact we’re doing — every time I do the big band thing I have fifteen men, I have six brass, five saxes and three rhythm, four rhythm sometimes when I add a guitar, and Sam comes out and does a scat thing that he and I play flute and clarinet.
I’m curious if you two were always good buddies?

Well we were always good buddies but we weren’t close enough to find out. I don’t mean close enough, I mean miles. The distance between us. Because for a long time he was out of New York and I came out here and he wound up going to Europe and he was a bigger name than I ever was, which is great. And then we got together out here because he moved out, and I tried to do what I could with him and we became buddies here. He’s eleven years my junior and you’ve got to take care of your brother. So and vice versa. So we have fun. He’s a fine player. There are a lot of things he can do that I wish I can do —

play piano and his ears are just phenomenal. He just has some fantastic things, so I’m in a little different era. So when we both play a lot of people think it might not fit. Both styles. But they do. We interweave and we each do our thing and it works. Because we’re both on this one as a matter of fact.
I think you’ll like that, yeah.
